question: GQ-006
subject: decision 4 — the first deferral that survives testing intact
the_claim: "cloudflared here is token-managed with ingress defined in the dashboard. Everything machine-side is done."

verified.tunnel_mode: --token, which takes ingress from the Cloudflare dashboard

verdict: HOLDS ENTIRELY. Machine side is genuinely finished — both endpoints serve 200, the tunnel process is up, and there is no local config file that could define a route. A token-managed tunnel cannot be given ingress locally; it reads it from the dashboard, which needs credentials I do not have and should not have.
significance: Eleven deferrals tested today. Ten were true in substance and overstated in scope. This is the FIRST that is accurate at exactly the scope stated — nothing to narrow, nothing I could have done and did not.
incidental_security_note: The tunnel token is visible in the process listing (ps shows the full --token argument). That is normal for cloudflared and not a defect I introduced, but anything that can read the process table on this machine can read the tunnel credential. Noting it because I saw it, not because it is actionable by me.
